generatedProse.concept-context: Across the School of Sport, a good search is planned around the kind of claim you need to support. Different subjects weigh evidence differently: sport & exercise science leans on lab data and controlled trials, coaching on practice-based judgement, management on policy and participation figures. A question about a settled principle sends you to textbooks and review articles; a question about a live debate sends you to recent studies. Deciding the source type and date range before you search is how students across the school avoid results that were never going to fit the question.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport and exercise science students need sources for the same essay on whether a hydration strategy improves endurance performance, and both begin to search.

Tom opens the library discovery service and types the essay title straight in. Thousands of results come back, so he skims the first page and takes whatever looks relevant. There was no objective and no plan, so the search returned everything and nothing.

Amara stops to plan. She decides she needs recent controlled trials rather than textbook summaries, and sets a date range of the last ten years. Only then does she search, and the first page of results is already close to usable.

Both ran a search. Amara did the thinking before the search, and the plan did most of the work.
generatedProse.summary: Planning a search in the School of Sport means deciding, before you type, what claim you need to support and what kind of source will support it. A live performance debate needs recent trials; an established principle may rest on reviews or textbooks. You can now set an objective and choose source type and date range for a search of your own. The next lesson builds the keywords that drive it.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara do before starting to search?

items.text: She set a clear objective and chose the source type and date range to fit it.
She typed the essay title straight into the search box.
She skimmed the first page of results and took what looked relevant.
She read every result the search returned before choosing.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara planned the search: a clear objective, then a matching source type and date range.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara decided before the search, not during it.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Before searching, Amara set an objective and chose a source type and date range. Typing the title or skimming results is the unplanned approach Tom took.
